solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Having these at Christmas is insane?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the paper tubes pulled at the Christmas table, which bang and hold a paper hat
second meaning: informal British slang for mad

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether pulling festive novelties at Christmas is a mad thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: Christmas crackers are a British table custom; 'crackers' is also everyday British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names festive party novelties and, as slang adjective, means mad or crazy.

clue.text: Hold discussion about one's evergreen

indicators.note: 'about' means going round, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to confer is to talk things over
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Talks are held about somebody's evergreen tree.
explanation.walkthrough: CONFER goes around I; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Most conifers, such as pines and firs, keep their needles all year, so they are evergreens.

clue.text: Arrange, being ill-intentioned, to get rid of Mike

indicators.note: getting rid of something means it is removed from the word

parts.note: malign means evil in intent
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A malicious plot is arranged to dispose of someone called Mike.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping M from MALIGN leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To align things is to set them in order or in a line, a synonym for arrange.

clue.text: Vital approval for four flats, for example

parts.note: a key factor is a vital one
a signature on a document shows approval

explanation.surface: Sounds like a property deal needing approval for four apartments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flats' looks like apartments; they are musical flats, and four of them mark A flat major.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the sharps or flats written at the start of a stave make up the key signature.

clue.text: One is defenceless on these, which the experienced know

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a beaten boxer is said to be 'on the ...' of the ring
second meaning: old hands 'know the ...' of a job

explanation.surface: A boxer pinned in the corner of the ring, a place veterans know well.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are idioms built on the cords around a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The cords of a boxing ring, plus the idioms meaning near defeat and understanding how things work.

clue.text: Not initially a polite address to woman or man

indicators.note: 'not initially' tells us to drop the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the courteous way to address a lady

explanation.surface: A note on etiquette about how to address a woman or a man politely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or man' looks like part of the etiquette; it is the definition, with 'or' as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam is the first man in Genesis, so his name stands for man generally.

clue.text: Proper to include son in lineage

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: decent behaviour is proper behaviour
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: It is only right that a son appears in the family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Descent is ancestry or line of origin, the same as lineage.

clue.text: Painter late in the morning rising

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: ten o'clock in the morning, a late-ish hour

explanation.surface: An artist sleeps in and gets up late in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was the French painter of Olympia and Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe.

clue.text: Deteriorate badly around noon: made to face another way

indicators.note: 'around' means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped about the other
something done badly is botched and out of order, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Things go badly downhill around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters of DETERIORATE are set around N.
explanation.definitionFit: Reorientated is the British form of reoriented: turned to point in a new direction.

clue.text: Loud number is by Yankee

parts.note: standard abbreviation for number
taken as written
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A loud song is performed by an American.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noisy makes a lot of sound, which is a plain synonym for loud.

clue.text: Some of the media, working, waste no time

parts.note: the press is the newspaper part of the media
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Journalists at work never waste a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To press on is to continue urgently without pausing, so you waste no time.

clue.text: Source of money shortly provides pleasure

indicators.note: 'shortly' asks for the word to be cut short by losing its final letter

parts.note: a fund is a pool of money to draw on

explanation.surface: Money soon brings enjoyment, says a cynic.
explanation.definitionFit: Fun is enjoyment or amusement, a close synonym for pleasure.

clue.text: Rebel is concealing name, demanding attention

indicators.note: something concealing another holds it inside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name
an urgent matter demands attention

explanation.surface: A rebel hides his identity while making urgent demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebel' looks like the subject concealing his name, but it is the definition; the rest is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is someone who rises in revolt against authority, a synonym for rebel.

clue.text: Object to being given another errand?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: feel bitter about something

explanation.surface: A put-upon helper complains about being dispatched on yet another errand.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as re-sent, someone sent out a second time; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel aggrieved by it, close to objecting to it.

clue.text: Disdained starter of salami: like some beef?

indicators.note: a starter is what comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter
corned beef is salt-cured beef

explanation.surface: A diner turned up their nose at a salami starter, wondering if it was beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a first course; it picks the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be scorned is to be treated with contempt, a synonym for disdained.

clue.text: Prepare leftovers: hot, consume fully

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
to eat up is to finish everything on the plate

explanation.surface: Instructions for leftovers: warm them and finish them off.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftovers are readied by warming them through again, which is what heating up means.

clue.text: Criticise a prophet, do we hear, for universal remedy

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: 'do we hear' points to what the words sound like when spoken

parts.note: a seer is a prophet, and the two words said together sound like the ending

explanation.surface: Mocking a prophet, it seems, cures everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed cure-all, a remedy for every ill.

clue.text: Not manage to think straight, so find nothing to go with gin

definitions.meaning: first meaning: be dazed or befuddled

definitions.text: find nothing to go with gin
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: have run out of the mixer, tonic

explanation.surface: A drinker, too muddled to think, discovers there is no tonic left for the gin.
explanation.walkthrough: In the literal sense 'it' stands for the mixer the gin goes with, as in gin and it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be dazed or drunk, and literally means to have none of something left.

clue.text: Curb ambition to take in animal film

indicators.note: the phrase takes in, or contains, the letters that run across the word break

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Advice to rein in one's ambitions in order to fit an animal movie in.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambi is the 1942 Disney cartoon about a young deer, a film about animals.

clue.text: Obese wife given a judicial opinion

parts.note: obese means very fat
W is the abbreviation for wife
taken as written

explanation.surface: An overweight wife receives a court's ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' that ends the wordplay is the same 'a' that begins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatwa is a legal ruling issued by an Islamic scholar on a point of religious law.

clue.text: Loaf and maybe some baked beans here

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... loaf, bread baked in a rectangular pan
second meaning: the can that baked beans come in

explanation.surface: A shopping list of bread and baked beans.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'tin' is a British name for a tin loaf, a sandwich loaf baked in a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a style of bread loaf and the metal can that holds beans.

clue.text: Backing group of musicians in joint

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a nonet is a group of nine musicians

explanation.surface: A backing band is playing in a smoky club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing group' reads as backing singers, but 'Backing' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is the projecting tongue of a mortise-and-tenon woodworking joint.

clue.text: Where one has an elevated religious calling

definitions.text: Where one has an elevated religious calling

parts.words: Where one has an elevated religious calling
parts.note: surface reading: a place for someone with a lofty spiritual vocation
setter's reading: a high tower from which the call to prayer is literally sung out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Calling' looks like a vocation, but here it is the call to prayer given from a tall tower beside a mosque.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque from which the muezzin calls the faithful to prayer.

clue.text: Jacket starts off the uniform, newly in colour

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are what we keep, one letter from each

parts.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A uniform jacket gets freshly coloured.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a close-fitting military or uniform jacket.

clue.text: Blowing hard, losing weight in a type of racing

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away from the word

parts.note: a windy day is one with the wind blowing hard
W is the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: Gusty conditions make the cars shed weight in motor racing.
explanation.walkthrough: W is taken out of WINDY.
explanation.definitionFit: Indy racing is a US open-wheel motorsport, named after the Indianapolis 500.

clue.text: Flower's unusual drainage

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener remarks on a bed with unusually good drainage.
explanation.definitionFit: The gardenia is a shrub with fragrant white blooms, an example of a flower.
